problems.what: the name 'borrowed adulthood', 'provisional', the familiar practices it combines; 'many of the steps have been shown to be effective' is new
problems.replace: To help these people access their adult functions, I recommend the following steps. Please note, the following is a bridge that I developed – while many of the steps have been shown to be effective, the entirety of the steps have not (to the best of my knowledge).
problems.with: For that starting point, I use a provisional bridge I developed and call borrowed adulthood. It puts together familiar practices (witnessing, modeling, supported action, and handing over responsibility bit by bit), but nobody has validated the whole sequence as one treatment, and I’m not claiming they have.

problems.with: If the younger part doesn’t believe you love it yet, you can still love it, when that love is there for you to give. Its trust can question your promises, remember the times you didn’t protect it, and take its time. The love can stay while that happens.

problems.what: that isn't a way to end the complaint; repair after an internal attack (the adult's own), not the child attacking; 'him/her'
problems.replace: Respond to complaints by hearing the truth in them and by responding to them, as well as by providing the other evidence of love: preparing and serving meals, setting limits to protect him/her, taking him/her to appointments, keeping promises, admitting when you haven’t been able to live up to your promises, etc. If the younger position attacks you in his/her mind, admit that you haven’t been able to protect him/her yet, work on it, and let him/her know when you’ve made a change. Show your love by not retaliating, but don’t substitute not retaliating for loving the younger position.
problems.with: That isn’t a way to end the complaint. Hear the truth in it and answer it seriously. Hearing anger without hitting back, admitting a real failure, and making repair after you’ve turned on the child inside are evidence too, alongside the meals, the limits that protect, the appointments and the kept promises. Show your love by not retaliating, but don’t substitute not retaliating for loving the younger part.

problems.what: 'ICW' and 'IC' aren't the guide's words; what turns decorative; trust begins when you handle the consequence ('deal with the fallout if you don't' is new)
problems.replace: It's important to note that lots of people do ICW but it's often fluffy brouhaha - they talk to their IC, but they don't actually do the things they need to in their adult life. So in order to build trust with your IC, you need to do the thing . And deal with the fallout if you don't.
problems.with: This is where inner-child work often turns into fluffy decoration - people talk lovingly to their inner child, but then send the destabilizing message, skip the meal, avoid the task, and break the promise. Trust begins when you actually handle the consequence.
